source: Q&A on EU Food Information for Consumers Regulation allergen provisions (FSA)
regulation: EU FIC No.1169/2011 and Food Information Regulations 2014 (FIR)

the_14_allergens.name: Cereals containing gluten
the_14_allergens.declaration_note: Specific cereal types listed in Annex II (e.g. wheat, barley) must be declared and emphasised individually, e.g. 'wheat' or 'barley', not just 'gluten'.

the_14_allergens.name: Crustaceans
the_14_allergens.declaration_note: May be declared by the general word 'crustaceans' rather than each specific species.

the_14_allergens.name: Fish
the_14_allergens.declaration_note: May be declared by the general word 'fish' (e.g. 'cod (fish)') rather than naming the species, unless the species itself is another allergen group (e.g. shellfish).

the_14_allergens.name: Peanuts
the_14_allergens.declaration_note: Peanuts are legumes, not tree nuts, and are declared as their own separate allergen category.

the_14_allergens.name: Soybeans (soya)
includes: soybeans and soya products, e.g. soya lecithin

the_14_allergens.name: Milk
the_14_allergens.declaration_note: Common dairy foods (cheese, cream, butter, yoghurt) are considered to clearly reference milk already. Less familiar products (fromage frais, Mascarpone, Quark) and milk derivatives (lactose, casein, whey) need explicit reference to milk, e.g. 'whey (milk)'.

the_14_allergens.name: Nuts
the_14_allergens.declaration_note: The specific nut type must be declared and emphasised, e.g. 'almonds', not just 'nuts'.

the_14_allergens.name: Sesame seeds
the_14_allergens.declaration_note: Declare as 'sesame' or 'sesame seed', e.g. tahini should be flagged as containing sesame.

the_14_allergens.name: Sulphur dioxide / sulphites
includes: preservative E220-E228, often in dried fruit and wine
the_14_allergens.declaration_note: Only declarable where added and present above 10mg/kg (or 10mg/L) in the finished product.

the_14_allergens.name: Lupin
includes: lupin flour/seeds, sometimes used in bread and pastries

the_14_allergens.name: Molluscs
the_14_allergens.declaration_note: May be declared by the general word 'molluscs'.

key_facts_for_schools_and_caterers: Institutional caterers (schools, hospitals, childminders) fall within scope of the allergen rules with no exemption.
Where the consumer cannot make their own safe food choice (e.g. a young child), the institution has a duty of care to identify pre-existing allergies and ensure suitable, safe food is provided.
In schools, practical identification methods include coloured wristbands or a photo of the child with allergy details visible to kitchen/serving staff.
Blanket statements like 'all our foods contain allergens' are not compliant; specific allergen information must be given for the food actually supplied.
'May Contain' precautionary labelling (cross-contamination risk) is voluntary and is NOT covered by the mandatory EU FIC rules, but should be used after a real risk assessment.
Around 5-8% of children in the UK have a food allergy, compared to 1-2% of adults; allergic reactions to food cause approximately 10 deaths per year in the UK.

An allergic reaction can be triggered by a very small amount of allergen (e.g. a single sesame seed, a fragment of peanut), so trace-level cross-contamination matters even when an allergen is not a deliberate ingredient.

common_intolerances_not_legally_classed_.name: Lactose intolerance
common_intolerances_not_legally_classed_.note: Not an immune-system allergy; it is a digestive intolerance to lactose (milk sugar). Still requires avoiding/limiting milk and lactose-containing products, but is mechanistically different from a milk allergy and reactions are not typically life-threatening.

common_intolerances_not_legally_classed_.name: Gluten intolerance / coeliac disease
common_intolerances_not_legally_classed_.note: Coeliac disease affects an estimated 1 in 100 people and requires strict avoidance of gluten-containing cereals (wheat, barley, rye, oats). 'Gluten-free' and 'very low gluten' claims are governed by separate legislation (EU Regulation No. 41/2009), not EU FIC directly.
